problem: Generative models for PDEs struggle to ensure generated samples satisfy physical constraints and admissibility conditions.
approach: Augments diffusion model sampling with physics-based guidance from PDE residuals and observational constraints, embedded in a Sequential Monte Carlo framework for scalable solving.
contribution: Produces PDE solution fields with lower numerical error than state-of-the-art generative methods across multiple benchmark systems.

problem: Test-time adaptation fails in long-horizon deployments due to gradient-driven representation collapse, not just noisy pseudo-labels.
approach: Identifies manifold erosion via spectral analysis, revealing high-rank gradients from mispredictions leak into stable low-rank safety subspace; proposes MGP to project gradients onto orthogonal complement to block leakage.
contribution: Achieves long-horizon stability on diverse TTA benchmarks where prior methods collapse.

problem: RL with verifiable rewards improves LLM reasoning on math tasks but narrows outcome diversity into low-probability solutions.
approach: Defines set-level diversity objective via kernelized similarity, derives leave-one-out marginal contributions, integrates as advantage shaping term in policy optimization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in both Pass@1 and Pass@K across model scales and benchmarks.

problem: Parameter-free stochastic optimization typically relies on unverifiable knowledge like problem-parameter bounds, blocking truly parameter-free methods.
approach: Proposes GRASP, a grid search framework with novel self-bounding analysis to determine parameter search ranges without oracle bounds.
contribution: Achieves fully parameter-free methods in non-convex and convex cases with near-optimal convergence rates up to logarithmic factors.

problem: ReLU networks have rescaling symmetries that affect training dynamics but lack principled exploitation methods.
approach: Builds on path-lifting framework to introduce geometrically motivated rescaling criterion using kernel alignment in path-lifting space with efficient alignment algorithm.
contribution: Demonstrates potential to speed up training through architecture-aware initialization and rescaling.

problem: Visual agents stop using tools despite achieving higher accuracy, suggesting tool-use collapse and misalignment between tool frequency and reasoning quality.
approach: Adds entropy regularization to encourage diverse rollout exploration during training; focuses on diversity rather than tool-use frequency.
contribution: Achieves best performance despite declining tool usage by improving exploration diversity.

problem: Extreme weather diagnosis requires multi-step reasoning and expert knowledge integration that standard agents cannot provide at scale.
approach: Proposes HVR-Met, a multi-agent system with Hypothesis-Verification-Replanning closed-loop mechanism; integrates domain expertise and introduces atomic-level benchmark.
contribution: Excels in complex extreme weather diagnostic scenarios.

problem: Looped language models exhibit performance collapse at deeper recurrence depths due to instability-effectiveness trade-off in latent dynamics.
approach: Frames reasoning as uncertainty reduction; proposes STARS training framework using Jacobian Spectral Radius Regularization with random loop sampling to constrain states toward asymptotically stable fixed points.
contribution: Achieves reliable test-time scaling with stable fixed-point convergence and improved peak performance on arithmetic and mathematical reasoning.

problem: Multimodal LLM judges anchor on narrative text over visual perception, leading to biased and non-verifiable evaluations when vision conflicts with text.
approach: Constructs Perceptually Perturbed Judgment Dataset with minimal counterfactuals isolating perceptual errors; trains unified framework combining GRPO-based reward with batch-ranking objective.
contribution: Substantially improves perceptual fidelity, ranking coherence, and alignment with human evaluation across MLLM-as-a-Judge benchmarks.

problem: RL struggles to scale to large combinatorial action spaces where policy gradient methods become inefficient.
approach: Frames policy update as distributional matching via policy mirror descent, training discrete diffusion model to replicate regularized target policy.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency and performance on DNA sequence generation, macro-actions, and multi-agent benchmarks; reveals FKL-RKL trade-off.

problem: Workflow-based data agents cannot achieve full autonomy in end-to-end data science due to reliance on predefined workflows.
approach: Proposes DeepAnalyze with curriculum-based agentic training emulating human data scientist learning trajectory; introduces data-grounded trajectory synthesis framework.
contribution: With 8B parameters, outperforms workflow-based agents built on advanced proprietary LLMs on 13 benchmarks; fully open-sourced.

problem: Adversarial attacks on VLMs show poor transferability because they exploit surrogate-specific artifacts rather than shared safety mechanisms.
approach: Identifies safety circuits via linear probing; proposes SCIA using dual-objective steering to suppress defensive circuits and amplify transferable circuits, plus contrastive semantic steering.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art in bypassing unseen black-box VLMs.

problem: Monocular 3D avatar generation requires balancing identity-critical facial micro-structures with fine-grained view-consistent textures.
approach: Two-stage framework: latent 3D diffusion model pretrained and finetuned on 35K curated avatar models for facial mesh; multi-view-aware texturing via 2D diffusion guided by mesh geometry.
contribution: Produces more coherent facial geometry and fine-grained view-consistent textures than existing baselines.

problem: Attention modeling remains fragmented across modalities and task formulations, failing to generalize across scenes and applications.
approach: Reformulates attention as cognitive entailment organized in general-to-specific hierarchy via language prompts with hyperbolic embeddings; unifies static and video attention via Fokker-Planck equation.
contribution: AAM outperforms state-of-the-art by average 6% on 16 benchmarks with 4× speedup in video inference.

problem: LLM pretraining is inefficient due to lack of locality inductive bias in self-attention and knowledge-computation coupling in MoE.
approach: Proposes LoKiFormer with Local Fusion Attention incorporating convolutional fusion to capture local patterns, and Knowledge Memory Module with parametric key-value memory decoupling storage from computation.
contribution: Converges 1.33x faster in pretraining than baseline models.

problem: Non-monotonic sequence generation models lack principled learning of insertion order and support for variable-length generation.
approach: Formalizes bijective correspondence between insertion trajectories and permutations; proposes Insertion Process (IP) learning where and what to insert and when to terminate via permutation-based variational inference.
contribution: Learning insertion order improves modeling quality and generalization on goal-conditioned planning and molecular string generation without canonical left-to-right structure.

problem: Standardized LLM benchmarks provide aggregated metrics that obscure fine-grained gaps in model competencies and benchmark coverage.
approach: Uses concept activations from sparse autoencoders to identify per-concept gaps automatically and unsupervised; compares across models and benchmarks.
contribution: Recovers previously documented model gaps and identifies novel gaps; automatically uncovers benchmark coverage gaps.

problem: Graph edit distance computation via matching-based methods suffers from correlated candidates leading to suboptimal solutions and inefficient extraction.
approach: Proposes DiffGED, first generative approach using diffusion models to generate multiple diverse node matching matrices simultaneously, extracting diverse mappings efficiently.
contribution: Generates diverse edit paths with accuracy comparable to exact solutions while running faster than existing hybrid approaches.

problem: LLMs struggle with numerical time series due to inefficient text-based representations and limited pretraining exposure to numerical data.
approach: Augments LLM with specialized time series perception via patch-based encoder-decoder; trains on 25B+ tokens of interleaved time series and text across diverse tasks unified as next-token prediction.
contribution: TsLLM integrates time series analysis with natural language reasoning on tasks requiring both; demonstrates strong zero-shot and few-shot performance.

problem: Heisenberg-limited continuous-variable Hamiltonian learning protocols are limited to low-order structures or vulnerable to noise in generic multi-mode settings.
approach: Introduces Displacement-Random Unitary Transformation (D-RUT), an active data acquisition protocol with number-preserving transformations that reduce finite-order bosonic Hamiltonian learning to polynomial recovery.
contribution: Achieves Heisenberg-limited total evolution time with robustness to SPAM errors; hierarchical multi-mode recovery with better statistical efficiency than simultaneous estimation.

problem: Discrete flow models lack convergence guarantees and comprehensive error analysis compared to well-studied diffusion models.
approach: Develops unified framework grounded in stochastic calculus via Girsanov-type theorem for CTMCs; analyzes both transition rate estimation error and early stopping error.
contribution: Establishes non-asymptotic error bounds for distribution estimation and derives faster total variation convergence rate with boundedness condition, yielding nearly optimal rate.

problem: Fairness in optimal transport matching requires balancing matching quality with fairness constraints on cross-group probabilities.
approach: Proposes modified Sinkhorn algorithm for perfectly fair transport plans; develops penalized OT problem with finite-sample guarantees and bilevel optimization to learn fair cost function.
contribution: Enables efficient computation of fair transport plans with theoretical guarantees and empirical validation of fairness-cost trade-offs.

problem: Existing multimodal jailbreak methods rely on brittle templates and expose only narrow vulnerability subsets in VLMs.
approach: Proposes VERA-V, a variational inference framework casting jailbreak discovery as learning joint posterior over text-image prompts; integrates typography prompts, diffusion-based images, and structured distractors.
contribution: Achieves up to 53.75% higher attack success rate over baselines on GPT-4o and other frontier VLMs.

problem: LLM-powered agents in cybersecurity lack principled refusal boundaries, risking harmful misuse in offensive security tasks.
approach: Establishes first framework for refusal boundaries defining principled criteria, task categories warranting refusal, and evaluation methodology for robustness.
contribution: Assesses current frontier models finding 6 of 8 refuse to identify vulnerabilities in real systems 0% of the time.

problem: 3D visual grounding assumes unambiguous language references, but practical applications involve ambiguous or insufficient human instructions.
approach: Proposes interactive grounding framework with multi-round question-answer interactions; model generates clarifying questions receiving human answers about object attributes and spatial relations.
contribution: Constructs AmbiRefer3D dataset with 47,085 samples and 141,255 QA dialogue annotations; establishes multi-round evaluation metrics.

problem: Visual-first vibe coding paradigms lack large-scale multimodal training data and evaluation benchmarks for diagram-to-code translation.
approach: Introduces M²C-INSTRUCT with 13.1M samples across 50+ languages for visual design interpretation; trains M²-CODER multilingual developer and M²EVAL benchmark.
contribution: 7B M²-CODER matches 70B+ models, validating dataset quality; enables visual-assisted programming infrastructure.

problem: Preference-based RL with trajectory-level feedback lacks general theory and efficient algorithms under function approximation.
approach: Proposes RTPQ algorithm and proves regret guarantee via Dual Episodic Eluder Dimension (DEED), capturing trajectory-level and comparative preference structure.
contribution: Achieves √T regret with DEED=O(dH) for linear MDPs yielding Õ(dH√T max(H^3/2, 1/κ)) bound, nearly optimal and recovering dueling bandits and standard RL as special cases.

problem: LLMs exhibit significant safety gaps across low-resource languages as guardrails from high-resource languages fail to transfer.
approach: Proposes training-free Sparse Weight Editing framework identifying safety neurons and formulating cross-lingual alignment as constrained linear transformation with null-space projection.
contribution: Significantly reduces Attack Success Rate across 8 languages and multiple model families with negligible impact on utility via single data-efficient calculation.

problem: Strategic classification assumes rational agents, but real-world manipulation deviates from rationality due to psychological biases.
approach: Formalizes behaviorally realistic strategic classification via prospect theory mechanisms: asymmetry between benefits/costs, reference-point dependence, probability distortion; proposes Pro-SF framework.
contribution: Pro-SF bridges machine learning and behavioral economics for more reliable strategic classification deployment.

problem: Muon matrix sign gradient updates show empirical gains but lack theoretical understanding of dynamics and scaling behavior.
approach: Studies Muon in linear associative memory with softmax retrieval and hierarchical frequency spectrum; shows Muon mitigates gradient descent's frequency imbalance via implicit preconditioner.
contribution: Proves exponential speedup in noiseless case and derives scaling law for noisy power-law spectrum; validates through synthetic and LLaMA pretraining.

problem: LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm inherits probabilistic failure modes when oversighting other probabilistic systems without guarantees.
approach: Proposes FormalJudge, neuro-symbolic framework with Formal-of-Thought: LLMs compile natural language requirements to formal specs, Dafny/Z3 prove compliance yielding mathematical guarantees.
contribution: Achieves 16.6% average improvement over LLM-as-a-Judge; weak-to-strong generalization with 7B achieving >90% deception detection from 72B agents; near-linear safety via iteration.

problem: Autoformalization evaluation provides only opaque binary verdicts without interpretable insight into failure modes or improvement paths.
approach: Introduces FormalRx diagnostic framework with SCI Error Taxonomy (28 categories); trains FormalRx-8B on 56,287 synthetic samples with fine-grained diagnostic annotations.
contribution: Achieves F1=0.88 (verdict), 0.71 (categorization), 0.75 (localization), 0.73 (correction), substantially outperforming baselines.

problem: Causal inference under high-dimensional covariates and multi-valued treatments fails when structural non-overlap exists between observational and experimental data.
approach: Proposes constrained joint estimation minimizing observational risk while enforcing identifying restrictions via orthogonal experimental moments; learns representations with penalized primal-dual algorithm.
contribution: Achieves gains over baselines on large-scale ride-hailing, matching models with significantly more RCT data.

problem: Continual semantic segmentation under joint class, domain, and label shifts causes overfitting and instability from few-shot supervision in heterogeneous environments.
approach: Introduces gradient-adaptive stabilization via parameter-wise gradient-scaled perturbations; leverages unlabeled data through semi-supervised learning and prototype-anchored supervision.
contribution: Consistent improvements over prior methods across class-incremental, domain-incremental, and few-shot regimes; exposes failure modes of existing approaches.

problem: RLVR improves math reasoning on some models even with spurious rewards uncorrelated or negatively correlated with correctness.
approach: Analyzes GRPO clipping bias amplifying high-prior pretraining behaviors; identifies code reasoning as amplifiable behavior in Qwen models.
contribution: Shows 21.4% gain on MATH-500 with random rewards nearly matching 29.1% with ground truth; highlights model-dependent effectiveness requiring diverse validation.

problem: LLMs struggle with spatial reasoning on material structure modeling, a core but least automated step in materials research.
approach: Introduces AtomWorld benchmark evaluating LLMs on ten fundamental atomic structure actions across four modelling categories with verifiable metrics.
contribution: Finds Gemini 2.5 Pro best overall but success drops sharply with complexity, particularly rotation <12%; recommends LLMs as copilots over autonomous agents.

problem: Spiking transformers lack spike-driven positional encoding methods, inheriting ANN-based approaches that undermine sparse computation benefits.
approach: Proposes SPE with Positional Encoding Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neuron incorporating position-dependent signals into thresholds, propagating via spike trains.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing SNN methods on 13 NLP benchmarks while preserving energy efficiency without additional parameters.

problem: Long-horizon reasoning incurs substantial computational overhead from test-time scaling; sparse attention degrades accuracy due to selection errors accumulating over generation.
approach: Proposes LessIsMore training-free sparse attention exploiting token importance stability across heads and layers via cross-head unified token selection and stable recency window.
contribution: Matches or improves accuracy while attending fewer tokens; achieves 1.6× end-to-end speedup and 1.72× sparse attention speedup with kernel optimizations.

problem: Existing 3D seismic fault detection models brittle under realistic domain shifts, masked by simplified physics data inadequate for deployment.
approach: Introduces SeisMark, large-scale benchmark merging procedural geology with diffusion-based synthesis for domain-realistic textured volumes.
contribution: Acts as rigorous discriminator distinguishing robust modern architecture from legacy models; establishes verifiable standard for trustworthy safety-critical subsurface AI.

problem: Applying rotary position encodings from LLMs and vision transformers to graph-structured data is underexplored.
approach: Rotates tokens depending on graph Laplacian spectrum to inject structural information; proposes Wave-Induced Rotary Encodings (WIRE) recovering regular RoPE on grids, asymptotically depending on effective resistance.
contribution: WIRE boosts synthetic and real-world graph learning performance; compatible with linear attention unlike bias-based relative encodings.
